q185.question: If an ascending pilgrim fails in the Deity adventure in Havona, what happens, and why is that failure not regarded as defeat?
q185.answer:
The ascending pilgrims passing through the seven circuits of Havona set out, circuit by circuit, on the "Deity adventure" of recognizing and attaining, in turn, the Infinite Spirit, the Eternal Son, and the Universal Father. The Urantia Book reveals that nearly all succeed in this adventure, but that occasionally a pilgrim fails to attain on the first attempt [26:8.4]. Yet this failure is by no means the end. The pilgrim who fails returns for a time to the universes of time to serve, then comes back to the same circuit and tries again, and on the second attempt he always succeeds [26:8.5].

The book sums up the attitude of heaven toward such an event in these words: "⟦Q 26:8.3⟧On Paradise, disappointment is never regarded as defeat; postponement is never looked upon as disgrace⟦/Q⟧" [26:8.3], and the apparent failures of time are never confused with the significant delays of eternity.

1. Who Fails, and Where

After the attainment of the Infinite Spirit there are no more examinations; the tests of the inner circles are the very performances of the pilgrims while in the embrace of the Deities, and advancement is determined purely by the spirituality of the individual [26:8.3]. Nearly all attain the Infinite Spirit, though pilgrims from the first superuniverse occasionally fail on the first attempt; those who actually fail in the search for the Son come almost entirely from the third and fifth superuniverses, and most of those who fail to attain the Father come from the sixth superuniverse [26:8.4]. The book regards this as pointing to good and sufficient reasons for these unavoidable delays [26:8.4]. The cause of failure lies not in the spirit itself but in some phase of the technique of approach or of the experiential background; the spirit of such candidates was wholly acceptable [26:10.3].

2. Right after Failure: Comfort on the Second Circle

Those who are unsuccessful in the first effort at Deity attainment are advanced directly to the second circle before being returned to superuniverse service, and there the counselors and advisers become the counselors and comforters of these disappointed pilgrims [26:10.2]. The book says that this disappointment differs in no way, except in its magnitude, from the long list of experiences on which they had climbed, as on a ladder, from chaos to glory [26:10.2]. After a long sojourn on the second circle they are examined by the councils of perfection and certified as having passed the Havona tests, and as regards their nonspirit status they receive the same standing as those who actually succeeded [26:10.3]. When a pilgrim who came to Havona alone fails, a Paradise Companion is assigned to accompany him, comforting and encouraging him until his return [25:8.9].

3. The Return to Service and the Second Adventure

The failing candidates are returned to the work of the realms of space for not less than one millennium, under the jurisdiction of the conductors of assignment of the primary supernaphim, going not to their native superuniverse but to the supercreation best suited for their retraining [26:8.5]. Led by their counselors, they stand before the conductors of assignment and return to the service of time, but they go in joy and gladness [26:10.4]. The author of the book testifies that he has observed them serving as the highest type of loving ministrators to those who experience temporary disappointments [26:10.2]. When their service is finished they return of their own accord to the outer circuit of Havona and prepare again from the circle where their career was interrupted; on the second attempt the same supernaphim ministers are with them, and these never fail to pilot their charges to success [26:8.5, 26:10.4].

4. Lessons for Our Spiritual Life

The book says that the pilgrim who reaches Havona already possesses a faith that disappointment cannot shake, so that even failure to discern the Universal Father cannot disturb that trust [26:4.13]. Long before coming to Havona they had learned "⟦Q 26:5.3⟧to feast upon uncertainty, to fatten upon disappointment⟦/Q⟧" [26:5.3] and to enthuse over apparent defeat. Their battle cry was that in liaison with God nothing is impossible [26:5.3]. The fact that in the event of failure no reasons are ever assigned, and that neither the candidates nor their tutors are ever chided or criticized [26:8.3], shows that heaven's way of dealing with failure is not judgment but patience and retraining.

Summary

The pilgrim who fails in the Deity adventure of Havona is comforted on the second circle and certified as having passed the tests, then serves joyfully in the worlds of space for not less than a millennium, and returns to succeed without fail on the second attempt [26:8.5, 26:10.2-10.4]. That failure is not a defect of spirit but only a "delay" arising from questions of technique and experience [26:10.3], and Paradise never regards disappointment as defeat or postponement as disgrace [26:8.3]. This teaching reminds us that the disappointments we meet now may also be one rung on the ladder of ascension.

q186.question: What is the meaning of the "last rest" that the ascending pilgrim enters on the final circuit of Havona, and what are the roles of the complements of rest and the instigators of rest?
q186.answer:
The mortal ascender falls into the last sleep of time on the innermost circuit of Havona and awakens to life everlasting on the shores of Paradise. The Urantia Book describes this sleep not as mere slumber but as a rest of metamorphosis that changes a "creature of time" into a "denizen of eternity" [27:1.3]. The beings who assist this decisive transition are the complements of rest, the last order of secondary supernaphim, and the instigators of rest, the first order of primary supernaphim [26:10.7, 27:1.1].

The book states the meaning of this transition thus: "⟦Q 26:11.8⟧Your first transition was indeed death, the second an ideal sleep, and now the third metamorphosis is the true rest⟦/Q⟧" [26:11.8], that is, the relaxation of the ages.

1. The Sevenfold Nature of Rest

The book explains that rest is of a sevenfold nature [27:1.2]. In the lower orders of life there is the rest of sleep and of play; in higher beings, the rest of discovery; and in the highest type of spirit personality, the rest of worship. There is also the rest of energy intake, the recharging with physical or spiritual energy, and the transit sleep when enseraphimed in passage from one sphere to another [27:1.2]. Entirely different from all of these is the deep sleep of metamorphosis, the transition rest from one state of existence to another, which always attends a change of actual universe status [27:1.2].

2. The Complements of Rest: Companions Who Keep You from Sleeping Alone

Much of the ascender's time on the last circuit is spent studying the problems of the impending Paradise residence, and the complements of rest help with adjustment to Paradise through association with the diverse groups of beings there [26:11.1, 26:11.3]. They are concerned less with the training of the pilgrims than with fostering understanding association among the various groups [26:11.3]. And when the time comes to sleep, you do not go alone to your rest as in the sleep of mortal death or in the transit trance to Havona [26:11.7]. Your long-time associate of the first circle, the complement of rest, moves over by your side and enters the rest as one with you; this is the pledge of Havona that your transition is complete and that only the final touches of perfection remain [26:11.7].

3. The Instigators of Rest: Those Who Induce the Sleep and Greet the Awakening

The instigators of rest are the inspectors of Paradise who go forth from the central Isle to the inner circuit of Havona to collaborate with the complements of rest [27:1.1]. The book says, "⟦Q 27:1.1⟧The one essential to the enjoyment of Paradise is rest, divine rest⟦/Q⟧" [27:1.1], and introduces them as the final instructors who make ready the pilgrims of time for eternity. They first meet the pilgrims toward the end of their sojourn on the first circle and complete the preparation for the transition sleep of the final resurrection [26:11.6]. On awakening in repersonalization on Paradise, the ascender at once recognizes that the instigator of rest who greets him on the shore is the very supernaphim who induced the last sleep [27:1.4].

4. The Door to Becoming a Child of Eternity

The book says that no one is truly a Paradise child until he has crossed the inner circuit and experienced the resurrection of eternity from the last sleep of time [26:11.6]. Only those who thus fall asleep on the first circle of Havona and awaken on the shores of Paradise are children of eternity; others go as guests without residential status [26:11.6]. Just as seraphim are indispensable to mortal survival, the instigators of rest and the complements of rest are indispensable to this transcending metamorphosis [27:1.3]. The awakened ascender remembers the last supreme stretch of faith with which he once more committed the keeping of his identity into the hands of the Universal Father [27:1.4].

Summary

The last rest on the inner circuit of Havona is the third transition, following death and the transit sleep; it is the sleep of metamorphosis that changes a creature of time and space into an eternal resident of Paradise [26:11.8, 27:1.3]. The complement of rest, as a long-time companion, sleeps alongside and pledges the completion of the transition, while the instigator of rest induces that sleep and greets the awakened one on the shores of eternity [26:11.7, 27:1.4]. The ascender entrusts himself to the Father in this sleep as a final act of faith, and then awakens to the life everlasting of which it is said: "⟦Q 27:1.5⟧And there shall be no more sleep⟦/Q⟧." [27:1.5]

q187.question: In the account of the conductors of worship on Paradise, what does The Urantia Book teach that worship is, and what does it mean for us now?
q187.answer:
Paper 27 of The Urantia Book, in introducing the conductors of worship, the seventh order of primary supernaphim, gives its clearest definition of the essence of worship. The book says, "⟦Q 27:7.1⟧L’adoration est le privilège suprême et le premier devoir de toutes les intelligences créées.⟦/Q⟧." [27:7.1], and explains that worship is the conscious and joyous act of recognizing and acknowledging the truth and fact of the intimate and personal relationships of the Creators with their creatures [27:7.1].

Worship, then, is at once a duty and a joy, an experience that grows larger and wider the more deeply one knows God. It would not be too much to say that the whole ascension career moves toward the fullness of this worship.

1. The Quality of Worship Depends on the Depth of Perception

The quality of worship is determined by the depth of creature perception, and as the knowledge of the infinite character of the Gods grows, the act of worship becomes increasingly all-encompassing [27:7.1]. In the end it attains the highest experiential delight and the most exquisite pleasure known to created beings [27:7.1]. As the circuits of Havona are passed one by one, worship becomes an ever-growing passion, until on Paradise it becomes necessary to direct and otherwise control its expression [27:7.2].

2. All of Paradise a Single Sanctuary

There are several places of worship on the Isle of Paradise, but the Isle itself is more like one vast sanctuary of divine service [27:7.2]. Worship is the first and dominant passion of all who climb up to its shores, the spontaneous effervescence of beings who have learned enough about God to attain his presence [27:7.2]. Even with set times and places of worship, these cannot accommodate the overflowing emotions of beings who have struggled up from the spiritual darkness of the lower worlds, and the book says that personalities perfect by nature can never fully appreciate their response [27:7.6].

3. What the Conductors of Worship Do

The outpourings of adoration and praise on Paradise take place under the direction of the conductors of worship [27:7.3]. Every ascending being would delight to remain forever in the attitude of worship, so the directors of assignment must periodically disperse the assemblies, and no ascending being is required to enter upon the assignments of eternal service until he has attained full satisfaction in worship [27:7.3]. The conductors of worship teach how to worship so as to gain the satisfaction of self-expression while still giving attention to the essential activities of Paradise; otherwise it would take the average mortal hundreds of years to express his full gratitude [27:7.4]. All the arts of the whole universe that can intensify self-expression and the conveyance of appreciation are employed in this worship [27:7.5].

4. The Fruit of Worship and the Corps of the Finality

When the hearts of the Gods are fully satisfied by the sincere worship of the residents, the light of the Deity abode flashes in threefold pulsations, and the book calls it the great fruit of the plan of the Gods that the intelligent love of the creature satisfies the infinite love of the Creator Father [27:7.7]. Only after attaining the supreme satisfaction of the fullness of worship is the ascender qualified for admission to the Corps of the Finality, and the seventh jubilee celebrates this [27:7.8]. The conductors of worship are the last supernaphim to bid farewell to the ascender when he takes the Trinity oath and is mustered into the Corps of Mortal Finaliters [27:7.9].

5. Worship Here and Now

The book says that the mode of worship on Paradise is beyond mortal comprehension, but that its spirit can begin to be appreciated even here on Urantia, because the spirits of the Gods even now indwell us, hover over us, and inspire us to true worship [27:7.5]. It also says, "⟦Q 27:7.5⟧Ce que le jeu fait pour votre mental surmené sur terre, l’adoration le fera pour votre âme rendue parfaite au Paradis.⟦/Q⟧." [27:7.5], showing that worship is a joy that brings new strength.

Summary

Worship as The Urantia Book describes it is the joyous acknowledgment of our personal relationship with God, the highest privilege and the first duty of all intelligences [27:7.1]. Worship deepens the more we know God, becomes the highest joy on Paradise, and only on attaining full satisfaction in worship does eternal service as a finaliter begin [27:7.3, 27:7.8]. Its spirit begins to grow even now on this earth through the spirit that indwells us [27:7.5].

q188.question: Unlike the ascenders who come and go in the local universe, who are the "permanent citizens" who always remain there, and why are they needed?
q188.answer:
The mortal ascender is a pilgrim who keeps moving onward, from the mansion worlds through Salvington to the superuniverse, and on to Havona and Paradise. But Paper 37 of The Urantia Book says that the local universe, like the superuniverse and the central universe, has its orders of "permanent citizenship" [37:9.1]. They are the Susatia, the Univitatia, the Material Sons, and the midway creatures, who, together with the Spirit-fused ascenders and the Spironga, make up a relatively permanent citizenry [37:9.2-9.6].

These beings, as a rule, neither ascend nor descend, but continually contribute to the universe the experience they have accumulated on the level of their origin [37:9.6]. Their part is to give continuity and experiential wisdom to a universe administration whose personnel is constantly changing.

1. The Permanent Residents of Each Administrative Unit

The book summarizes that every division of the administrative organization has its residents of citizenship status [37:9.12]. Urantia has its midwayers; Jerusem, the system capital, has its Material Sons and Daughters; Edentia, the constellation headquarters, has its Univitatia; and the citizens of Salvington are of two kinds, the created Susatia and the evolved Spirit-fused mortals [37:9.12]. Uversa, the superuniverse headquarters, has its Abandonters; Havona has its native beings; and Paradise has its Paradise Citizens [37:9.12].

2. The Susatia and the Univitatia

The Susatia are the glorious offspring of the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit; they reside on Salvington as permanent citizens and are closely associated with the Spirit-fused mortals of the Nebadon corps of perfection [37:9.7]. The Univitatia are nonreproducing beings who minister on the one hundred constellation headquarters spheres, existing on a plane of life about midway between the semimaterial status of the Material Sons and the spirit level of the Susatia [37:9.8]. The book says that the Univitatia do for the ascending mortals passing through the constellation spheres what the Havona natives do for the pilgrims of the central universe [37:9.8].

3. The Material Sons and the Midway Creatures

The Material Sons and Daughters are the reproducing order of sonship created by the Creator Son as he personalizes his final concept of being in dual form; their offspring live as permanent citizens of the system capitals, and some are commissioned as Planetary Adams [37:9.9]. The midway creatures are the only group of intelligent beings who remain continuously on a planet from the days of the Planetary Prince to the far-distant time of its settling in light and life [37:9.11]. We mortals are short-lived residents who are born, live, die, and pass on to other worlds, and the assignments of celestial ministers are also transient; but the book says, "⟦Q 37:9.11⟧On Urantia the midway ministers are in reality the actual custodians of the planet⟦/Q⟧" [37:9.11], and explains that they provide continuity of planetary administration.

4. The Spirit-fused Mortals: Evolved Permanent Citizens

The Spirit-fused mortals, the other citizens of Salvington, do not attain Paradise, but in dealing with the problems of Nebadon they achieve an experiential wisdom surpassing anything attained by the ascenders who are passing through [37:5.11]. Those of them who become High Commissioners begin as racial commissioners on the planets, representing the viewpoints and needs of the human races, and act as advisers in all tribunals [37:5.5, 37:5.7]. The book says that "⟦Q 37:5.9⟧they are always present to speak for those who cannot be present to speak for themselves⟦/Q⟧" [37:5.9].

5. Why Permanent Citizens Are Needed

The book explains that the plan limiting the ascent of Spirit-fused mortals benefits the local universe by insuring it a permanent evolutionary population that will continue to stabilize and diversify local universe administration with ever-increasing experience [37:5.11]. If all mortals departed for Paradise, the local universe and superuniverse tribunals would depend solely on the service of those who are passing through, so it is entirely fitting that there be a permanent ascending citizenry [40:10.4]. The authoritative wisdom that ripens in the faithful service of such local universe citizens is a decisive factor in the settling of a local universe [40:10.6].

Summary

The permanent citizens of the local universe are the Susatia and the Spirit-fused mortals of Salvington, the Univitatia of Edentia, the Material Sons and Daughters of Jerusem, and the midway creatures of the planets [37:9.2-9.5, 37:9.12]. While the ascenders keep passing through, these remain in their places and provide continuity of administration and experiential wisdom [37:9.6, 37:9.11], and thanks to them the local universe can at last be settled in light and life [37:5.11, 40:10.6].

q189.question: Please explain in order the "seven stages of the ascending mortal" set out in Paper 30 of The Urantia Book, from the planet to Paradise.
q189.answer:
Section 4 of Paper 30 summarizes in seven stages the universe career of an Adjuster-indwelt mortal from birth on a planet to arrival on Paradise. The seven stages are: planetary mortals, sleeping survivors, mansion world students, morontia progressors, superuniverse wards, Havona pilgrims, and Paradise arrivals [30:4.2-4.8]. The book tells this story with reference to Adjuster-fused mortals, explaining that all the races of Urantia may look forward to such a destiny [30:4.9].

In terms of bodily form, these seven stages are a journey of transformation from a creature of flesh and blood to a morontia being, and then from an evolving spirit to a perfected spirit [30:4.26].

1. Planetary Mortals and Sleeping Survivors

All mortals are evolutionary beings of animal origin with ascendant potential, and the human races of every world enjoy the same ministry of the Sons of God and the presence of the ministering spirits [30:4.10]. Among mortals of survival status, those who have attained the level that merits personal guardians are personalized on the mansion worlds in the third period, but the others rest in unconscious sleep until the coming of a Son of God at the end of the dispensation [30:4.11]. To these sleepers the passing of time is of no consequence; one who has slept five thousand years reacts no differently from one who has rested five days [30:4.12].

2. Mansion World Students and the Resurrection

All survivors who reawaken on the mansion worlds are mansion world students [30:4.14]. The physical body returns to the earth; the Adjuster keeps the spirit transcript of the mind, and the seraphim keep the immortal soul, and the resurrection takes place when the two reassemble what they hold in trust [30:4.15]. Each local system, made up of about one thousand inhabited planets, has seven mansion worlds [30:4.16], and it was to such training worlds that Jesus referred when he said, "⟦Q 30:4.17⟧In my Father's house are many mansions⟦/Q⟧." [30:4.17]

3. Morontia Progressors

While ascending from the mansion worlds through the spheres of the system, the constellation, and the local universe, mortals are called morontia progressors, and they serve in various assignments together with their teachers and older brethren [30:4.18]. Throughout this period they are wards of the local universe [30:4.19]. Just before leaving the local universe headquarters they attain true spirit identity; this is only a minor transition, for mind, personality, and character are unchanged, and only the form is altered [30:4.20]. At this time they receive spirit confirmation from the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit, and no superuniverse ward has ever been known to go astray [30:4.21].

4. Superuniverse Wards and Havona Pilgrims

On arriving at the training worlds of the superuniverse, the ascender becomes a ward of the Ancients of Days, climbs through the cultural spheres of the minor sectors, the major sectors, and the superuniverse headquarters, and thoroughly learns local universe and superuniverse administration [30:4.22-4.24]. When spirit development is complete, he prepares for the long flight to Havona; this journey is always made alone, and from here on instruction is personal and individual [30:4.26, 30:4.27]. The first act of the Havona career is to thank the transport seconaphim, and then to send a message of gratitude and adoration to the Creator Son [30:4.28].

5. Paradise Arrivals

Residence on Paradise means that one has found God and will be mustered into the Mortal Corps of the Finality [30:4.31]. After a period of liberty the arrivals associate with the seven groups of primary supernaphim, and on completing the course with the conductors of worship they are assigned, as Paradise graduates, to finaliter service [30:4.32]. The book says that their present destiny alone fully justifies the universe plan of evolutionary ascension [30:4.33].

Summary

The mortal ascender begins as a planetary mortal and, if necessary, passes through the stage of sleeping survivor, then advances as mansion world student, morontia progressor, superuniverse ward, Havona pilgrim, and Paradise arrival [30:4.2-4.8]. Along the way the body changes from material to morontia to spirit, while mind, personality, and character continue [30:4.20, 30:4.26]; this outline is the average plan in effect in Nebadon and Orvonton [30:4.34].

q190.question: Besides ascended mortals, what beings make up the Mortal Corps of the Finality, and how is a single company organized?
q190.answer:
The Urantia Book introduces the Mortal Corps of the Finality as the present known destination of the ascending Adjuster-fused mortals of time, while making clear that this corps is not made up of mortals alone [31:0.1]. The primary Corps of the Finality consists of six groups, Havona natives, Gravity Messengers, glorified mortals, adopted seraphim, glorified Material Sons, and glorified midway creatures, and the seventh place is still vacant [31:0.2-0.8, 31:7.3].

These diverse beings are organized according to their experience of working together during the ascension career; all are received on an equal footing, but that equality does not abrogate individuality or personal identity [31:0.9].

1. The Organization of a Company

The corps is organized in companies of one thousand, consisting of one Havona native, one Gravity Messenger, and nine hundred and ninety-seven ascendant creatures [31:1.3]. Of these, the Adjuster-fused mortals and the adopted seraphim usually make up nine hundred and ninety, the mortals far outnumbering the seraphim [31:3.1]. There are just ten places in each company for beings who are neither mortals nor seraphim: the Havona natives, the Material Sons, the midway creatures, the Gravity Messengers, and the unknown member [31:3.1]. At present every company has nine hundred and ninety-nine sworn permanent members, and the vacancy is temporarily filled by the chief of the Evangels of Light [31:7.1].

2. The Havona Natives and the Gravity Messengers

The Mortal Corps of the Finality admits as permanent members only beings who have fused with the spirit of the Father, or beings like the Gravity Messengers who inherently embody that spirit [31:1.2]. The Havona natives must therefore achieve, in liaison with evolutionary beings, the experiential development that creates capacity to receive a fragment of the Father's spirit, and they are received in the ratio of one to a thousand [31:1.2, 31:1.3]. The possibility of becoming finaliters is one of the supreme adventures of this perfect race [31:1.4]. The Gravity Messengers are modified and personalized Adjusters from Divinington, superspirit beings who seem to utilize all energies and circuits, even gravity [31:2.2]. They are under the command of the finaliters, and between them and the mortal finaliters fused with fragments of the Father there is profound mutual affection [31:2.1, 31:2.4].

3. The Adopted Seraphim, the Material Sons, and the Midway Creatures

Many of the faithful seraphic guardians of mortals pass through the ascension career with their wards, become Father fused, take the finaliter oath together with them, and forever accept the destiny of their mortal associates [31:4.1]. Material Sons may embark on the ascent by petition when their planetary assignment is long delayed, or may become humanized, receive Adjusters, and ascend in the later ages of light and life; when they are in a finaliter company they are always chosen as leaders [31:5.1-5.3]. The midway creatures begin their ascent after their native world has been settled in light and life, and the secondary midwayers all eventually fuse with Adjusters and are mustered into the mortal corps [31:6.1, 31:6.2].

4. The Evangels of Light and the Vacant Seventh Place

Any celestial personality assigned to the service of the Corps of the Finality is called an Evangel of Light; these are temporary members who do not take the finaliter oath [31:7.2]. There are at present just six classes of permanent members, and as to the identity of the seventh group, even the beings on Uversa can only offer various speculations [31:7.3-7.5]. The finaliters are a self-governing body that chooses its own leaders, and they swear allegiance only to the Paradise Trinity [31:0.12]. The book calls them the tried and true souls of time and space, "⟦Q 31:0.13⟧the evolutionary salt of the universe⟦/Q⟧" [31:0.13].

Summary

The Mortal Corps of the Finality is made up mostly of Adjuster-fused mortals and adopted seraphim, together with Havona natives, Gravity Messengers, and glorified Material Sons and midway creatures, while the seventh place for permanent members is still vacant [31:0.2-0.8, 31:3.1, 31:7.3]. A company numbers one thousand, filled by nine hundred and ninety-nine permanent members and the chief of the Evangels of Light as a temporary member [31:1.3, 31:7.1]. What characterizes this corps is that beings of different origins form one body on an equal footing while each keeps his own identity [31:0.9].

q191.question: Why did God not make human beings perfect from the start, but have them evolve and ascend from lowly beginnings?
q191.answer:
Paper 32 of The Urantia Book answers this question head-on. It would have been just as easy for the Universal Father to make all mortals perfect beings and to impart perfection by his word, but that would deprive them of "⟦Q 32:3.11⟧the wonderful experience of the adventure and training associated with the long and gradual inward climb⟦/Q⟧" [32:3.11]. That experience is to be had only by those who begin at the very bottom of living existence [32:3.11].

Evolution, then, is not a sign of God's incapacity or indifference but a way that reveals the wisdom of the Creators [32:3.11], and the whole universe is designed so that the creatures who "receive" perfection and the creatures who "achieve" perfection complement each other [32:3.12].

1. Outside Havona, Perfection Is Achieved Progressively

The only settled creation is Havona, made directly by the thought of the Universal Father and the word of the Eternal Son, while the seven superuniverses are finite, evolutionary, and steadily progressive [32:3.1]. The physical systems of time and space are all evolutionary in origin [32:3.2], and except for the central universe, perfection is a progressive attainment [32:3.3]. Havona holds the pattern of perfection, and all other realms must attain that perfection by the established methods [32:3.3].

2. Acquired Perfection Is a Bona Fide Personal Possession

The book says that the perfection achieved by the creatures of time is "⟦Q 32:3.9⟧wholly an acquirement, a bona fide personality possession⟦/Q⟧" [32:3.9]. Though the elements of grace are freely admixed, the attainment is the result of individual effort and actual living, the reaction of personality to the existing environment [32:3.9]. Thus the fact of animal evolutionary origin attaches no stigma to any personality, and those who begin at the bottom and climb the ladder rung by rung receive greater honor and an actual knowledge of every phase of life [32:3.10]. There is truly no limit to the spiritual ascent of those who are indwelt by the Mystery Monitors [32:3.8].

3. The Mutual Complement of Inborn and Evolved Perfection

The experiential nature of evolving personalities is the natural complement of the ever-perfect nature of the Paradise-Havona creatures [32:3.12]. Perfect creatures and perfected creatures are both incomplete in finite totality, but when they are associated together they escape their inherent limitations [32:3.12]. The two are alike in degree of divinity potential but differ in kind, and each must depend on the other to attain supremacy of service [32:3.14]. Inborn perfection and evolved perfection are co-ordinate, dependent, and integrated [32:3.15].

4. The Eternal Purpose within Evolution

There is a great and glorious purpose in the march of the universes through space, and none of the struggles of mortals are in vain [32:5.1]. The events of time and the struggles of material existence are but the transient scaffolding that bridges over to spiritual realities [32:5.2]. In the mind of God there is a plan that embraces every creature, and this plan is "⟦Q 32:5.7⟧an eternal purpose of boundless opportunity, unlimited progress, and endless life⟦/Q⟧" [32:5.7]. Yet because in the lower stages of progress it is difficult to find the invisible Father with the eyes of faith, the book counsels that the surest safeguard is to hold persistently to the truth that the Father is present in his Sons [32:3.6].

5. What It Means for Our Lives

This teaching shows us that the immaturity and struggle we experience are not signs of failure but the process by which perfection becomes "our own." The book promises that the race for perfection is on, that whosoever will may enter, and that the crown of victory will be placed on every effort to run the race of faith in reliance on the guidance of the indwelling Adjuster and the Spirit of Truth [32:5.8].

Summary

God did not make us perfect from the start in order to give us the adventure and training of beginning at the bottom and acquiring perfection through experience [32:3.11]. The perfection thus gained is a bona fide personal possession [32:3.9], and in partnership with the inborn perfection of Havona it fulfills the larger purpose of the universe [32:3.12, 32:3.15]. The path of evolution is a journey that is not in vain within the eternal plan of God [32:5.1, 32:5.7].

q192.question: In the administration of the local universe of Nebadon, what position does each of Michael, Gabriel, and Immanuel hold, and what does each do?
q192.answer:
Paper 33 of The Urantia Book explains the government of our local universe of Nebadon around three personalities. Michael of Nebadon, the Creator Son, is the sovereign who chose to organize this universe and now supremely rules it [33:2.2]; Gabriel of Salvington, the Bright and Morning Star, is the chief executive of Nebadon [33:4.5]; and Immanuel of Salvington, the Union of Days, is the ambassador of the Paradise Trinity [33:5.1].

Put simply, Michael rules, Gabriel executes, and Immanuel represents Paradise and counsels. Knowing the relationship among the three lets us see how the local universe runs in good order.

1. Michael: Sovereign and Personification of the Father-Son

Michael's personal power is limited only by the gravity circuits centering in Paradise and by the reservation of the Ancients of Days of final judgment regarding the extinction of personality [33:2.2]. The book says, "⟦Q 33:2.3⟧Michael is the personification of the Paradise Father-Son to and in the local universe of Nebadon⟦/Q⟧" [33:2.3]. When he returned from his final bestowal on Urantia and the Mother Spirit subordinated herself to him, he acquired jurisdiction over all power in heaven and on earth [33:2.3]. His creature bestowal experience qualified him to portray the experiential divinity of the Supreme Being, and no other being has such qualifications for sole sovereignty [33:2.4]. He has his headquarters on Salvington, but he frequently visits the constellations, the systems, and even individual planets [33:2.5].

2. Gabriel: First-born Son and Chief Executive

Gabriel was created by the first joint act of the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit, and only one such being is brought forth in each local universe [33:4.1, 33:4.2]. He is like the Universe Son in divinity of nature but considerably limited in Deity attributes [33:4.2], and he embodies both the divine will of the Son and the creative imagination of the Spirit [33:4.3]. He is not a creator but a marvelous administrator, and apart from creation and life impartation, the Son and the Spirit never confer about important procedures without Gabriel [33:4.4]. He is the executive of superuniverse mandates and the commander in chief of the "hosts of heaven" [33:4.6], and when Michael is absent from Salvington he functions as regent [33:2.5]. During Michael's bestowals he became the director of actual universe affairs, and he has been closely connected with the history of Urantia [33:4.7].

3. Immanuel: Ambassador of the Trinity

The local universe is under the dual supervision of the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit, yet it is also blessed by the presence of personalities from Paradise, at whose head is Immanuel [33:5.1]. He is also the personal representative of the Universal Father to the court of the Creator Son, hence his name, Immanuel [33:5.1]. He is so humble that he declines the worship and adoration of all creatures; he is the only personality in Nebadon who has never acknowledged subordination to Michael, yet he counsels only when requested [33:5.2]. He is not under the jurisdiction of the local universe government, and he exercises no executive authority except in supervising the Faithfuls of Days of the constellations [33:5.3, 33:5.4].

4. The Balance Formed by the Three Personalities

During Michael's bestowals Gabriel always carried out the will of the incarnated Son and, with the co-operation of Immanuel, directed universe affairs [33:4.7]. Mortals rarely meet Gabriel during their ascent, but whoever becomes an administrator, of whatever order, comes under his direction [33:4.8]. Thus it is characteristic of the administration of Nebadon that sovereignty, execution, and the counsel of Paradise are distinct from one another yet work together.

Summary

In Nebadon, Michael is the sovereign who personifies the Father-Son [33:2.3]; Gabriel, as the first offspring of the Son and the Spirit, is the chief executive and regent of the universe [33:4.5, 33:2.5]; and Immanuel, as ambassador of the Trinity, is the humble Paradise representative who counsels only when requested [33:5.1, 33:5.2]. The co-operation of the three shows that the local universe is governed in good order under the love of the Creator and the wisdom of Paradise.

q193.question: Why does Michael the Creator not sit in judgment himself, and how are the tribunals of the local universe and the adjudication of eternal life carried out?
q193.answer:
The Urantia Book says that Michael, the Master Son of Nebadon, is concerned with only three things, creation, sustenance, and ministry, and that he does not personally participate in the judicial work of the universe. The book gives the reason briefly: "⟦Q 33:7.1⟧Creators never sit in judgment on their creatures⟦/Q⟧" [33:7.1]. Judgment is the exclusive function of creatures of high training and actual creature experience [33:7.1].

The tribunals of the local universe also have clear limits, and cases involving eternal life and death are taken up by the tribunals of the superuniverse of Orvonton [33:7.4]. This division shows that God's justice is always tempered by mercy and is never in haste [2:3.2].

1. The Judicial Machinery of Nebadon

All the judicial machinery of Nebadon is under the supervision of Gabriel, and the high courts of Salvington deal with matters of general universe importance and with appeals from the system tribunals [33:7.2]. These courts have seventy branches, and every case under adjudication is presided over by a dual judiciary consisting of a judge of perfect antecedents and a magistrate of ascendant experience [33:7.2]. That is, the viewpoint of perfection and the viewpoint of evolutionary experience take part together in judgment. There is no true legislative body on Salvington; legislation belongs to the constellation assemblies and execution to the systems [33:8.1].

2. Three Limits on the Local Universe Tribunals

First, the question of the right of continued existence, that is, of eternal life, must be referred to the tribunals of Orvonton, and if it is decided adversely, the sentence of extinction is executed through the agencies of the rulers of the supergovernment [33:7.4]. Second, defaults that jeopardize the status of the local universe Sons are adjudicated not by the tribunals of the Son but by the superuniverse tribunals [33:7.5]. Third, the readmission of a system that has been isolated requires the consent of the high council of the superuniverse [33:7.6]. In all other matters the decisions of the Salvington courts are final [33:7.7]. Michael's sovereignty is likewise limited in that the Ancients of Days reserve final judgment regarding the extinction of personality [33:2.2].

3. The Mercy Memory: Testimony Read before the Verdict

When an individual's right to unending life is up for adjudication in the courts of Uversa, the mercy memory of the tertiary seconaphim is read as testimony [28:6.6]. The Sons of God, by revealing the pre-existent mercy of the Father, establish the credit necessary for the survival of all, and that mercy credit is sufficient to insure the survival of every soul that truly desires divine citizenship [28:6.5]. The book says that if motives are honest and the heart sincere, the drawing credits of an individual far exceed his ability to exhaust that reserve [28:6.7]. Yet mercy is not forced upon those who despise it, and when mercy is exhausted, justice decides [28:6.7].

4. Extinction Is Not Hurried

The inevitable result of deliberate rebellion is the loss of existence, but the actual extinction is always delayed until the ordained order of justice has been fully complied with [2:3.2]. Extinction is usually decreed at the dispensational adjudication, by concerted action proceeding from the planetary council through the courts of the Creator Son to the tribunals of the Ancients of Days [2:3.3]. The rule of the Creator Sons is devoted to the rehabilitation of rebels, and extinction is executed only when every loving effort has been finally rejected [2:3.6].

Summary

The Creator does not sit in judgment on his creatures, and in Nebadon judgment is carried out under Gabriel's supervision by a judge of perfect antecedents together with a magistrate of experience [33:7.1, 33:7.2]. Questions of eternal life and extinction are decided by the tribunals of Orvonton after hearing the testimony of the mercy memory [33:7.4, 28:6.6]. The book comforts us that however unfair earthly judgments may sometimes appear, "⟦Q 33:7.8⟧in the universe justice and divine equity do prevail⟦/Q⟧" [33:7.8], so that we may trust we will be dealt with justly, even mercifully.

q194.question: If the Holy Spirit, the Spirit of Truth, and the Thought Adjuster are all present together in one person, how do these several spirits differ, and how do they work as one?
q194.answer:
Paper 34 of The Urantia Book says that there are three spirit presences in or with an evolving mortal: the Holy Spirit of the Universe Daughter of the Infinite Spirit (the local universe Mother Spirit), the Spirit of Truth of the Universe Son of the Eternal Son (the Creator Son), and the Adjuster-spirit of the Paradise Father. The presence of these three denotes "⟦Q 34:5.7⟧symmetry of spiritual endowment and ministry⟦/Q⟧" [34:5.7] and qualifies such a person consciously to realize the faith-fact of sonship with God [34:5.7].

Yet the book does not regard this as three spirits working separately. It stresses that although their origins are many, in human experience all spiritual influences are one in function [34:6.2].

1. The Holy Spirit: The Mother Spirit's Ministry, the First to Come

The Mother Spirit guides evolution, from lifeless matter through plants and animals to man, by means of the seven adjutant mind-spirits [34:5.2], and the mortal mind first experiences the ministry of spirit when it becomes receptive to the sixth and seventh adjutants, the adjutants of worship and wisdom [34:5.3]. Such a mind is soon included in the spiritual circuits of the Divine Minister and becomes able to choose a Thought Adjuster [34:5.3, 34:5.4]. The Holy Spirit is in part independent of human attitude and in part conditioned by the co-operation of the human will, and it increasingly sanctifies the inner life of those who follow divine leading [34:5.5].

2. The Spirit of Truth: The Bestowal Spirit of the Son

The Spirit of Truth is the spirit released by a bestowal Son, and before that time not all normal minds are automatically prepared to receive Adjusters [34:5.4]. The Spirit of Truth works as one with the Mother Spirit, and this dual spirit teaches truth and enlightens the mind [34:5.4]. The Spirit of Truth is poured out upon all flesh, but its function and power are limited almost wholly by man's personal reception [34:5.5]. The book encourages us that at every crossroad the Spirit of Truth will say, "⟦Q 34:7.8⟧This is the way⟦/Q⟧" [34:7.8].

3. The Thought Adjuster: The Father's Indwelling Fragment

The ministry of the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit does not indwell the thought center of the individual mind as the Adjuster does, and we do not possess detached portions of them [34:5.6]. The Adjuster, by contrast, is a definite individualization of the prepersonal reality of the Universal Father; it indwells the mortal mind and works in perfect harmony with the combined spirits of the Son and the Spirit [34:5.6]. Interpreting a scriptural passage, the book explains that because the Adjuster has already told us of our kinship to God, the Spirit bears witness "with your spirit" [34:6.12].

4. Spirits That Are One in Function

The book says that although Deity may be plural in manifestation, in human experience Deity is singular and always one [34:6.2]. As we progress spiritually, this multiple spirit ministry becomes increasingly co-ordinated and blended with the superministry of the Paradise Trinity [34:6.1], and as creatures receive this unifying ministry, it becomes in their experience the ministry of God the Supreme [34:6.2]. The spirit never drives but only leads, and every step we take must be one of willing co-operation [34:6.11].

5. A Union Revealed in the Fruits of the Spirit

A life led by the spirit is revealed in the fruits of the spirit, such as love, joy, and peace [34:6.13]. The book says that the seeds of theoretical truth are dead until the divine spirit breathes into them [34:6.6], and that it is not enough for the spirit to be poured out; it must dominate every phase of human experience [34:6.7]. Within us there exists "⟦Q 34:6.9⟧a conspiracy of spiritual forces, a confederation of divine powers⟦/Q⟧" [34:6.9] that seeks to deliver us from material bondage.

Summary

The Holy Spirit, as the ministry of the Mother Spirit, opens the mind to spirit; the Spirit of Truth, as the spirit of the bestowal Son, teaches truth; and the Thought Adjuster, as a fragment of the Father, indwells the mind [34:5.4-5.7]. Their origins are three, but in human experience these spirits are one in function [34:6.2], and without coercion, through our willing co-operation, they lead us to the consciousness of sonship with God and to the fruits of the spirit [34:6.11, 34:6.13].

q195.question: Why do the people of Urantia suffer so severely from the "warfare between the spirit and the flesh," and how can that warfare be won?
q195.answer:
Section 7 of Paper 34 of The Urantia Book deals directly with the inner conflict we feel every day, the warfare between our animal nature and our spiritual aspirations. The book says that every mortal has a dual nature: the inheritance of animal tendencies and the high urge of spirit endowment [34:6.9]. But it explains that this conflict is not normally as intense as it now is on Urantia, and that it is so because of two disasters our planet has suffered [34:7.4].

The book also clearly shows the way to win this warfare. It is not an asceticism that hates the flesh, but a life of faith that enters the spirit kingdom and does the will of God [34:7.6].

1. On a Normal World It Is "Education," Not "War"

Mortals living on normal worlds of spiritual progress do not experience the intense conflict between spirit and flesh that characterizes the present-day races of Urantia [34:7.2]. They too must climb from the animal levels to spiritual living, but the book says that this ascent is "⟦Q 34:7.3⟧more like undergoing an educational training⟦/Q⟧" [34:7.3] rather than an intense conflict. Even on the most ideal planets, however, pre-Adamic man must make a positive effort to ascend to higher values [34:7.2].

2. The Double Deprivation Urantia Has Suffered

The peoples of Urantia have been doubly deprived of help [34:7.4]. First, the Caligastia upheaval brought worldwide confusion and robbed all subsequent generations of the moral support that a well-ordered society would have provided [34:7.4]. Second, and more disastrous, was the Adamic default, which deprived the races of that superior type of physical nature which would have been more consonant with spiritual aspirations [34:7.4]. It was the divine plan that the races of Urantia should have a physical nature more naturally responsive to spirit [34:7.5]. For when the nature is upstepped by the addition of the nature of the Material Sons, the way is better prepared for the Spirit of Truth to co-operate with the Adjuster in yielding the fruits of the spirit [34:7.1].

3. The Desires of the Flesh Are Not in Themselves Sin

The book states plainly that the normal urges of animal creatures and the natural appetites of the physical nature are not in conflict with even the highest spiritual attainment [34:7.7]. They seem to conflict only in the minds of persons who are ignorant, mistaught, or unfortunately overconscientious [34:7.7]. We must live our material lives and cannot escape the body and its necessities, but in purpose and ideals we are increasingly empowered to subject the animal nature to the mastery of the spirit [34:6.9].

4. The Way to Win: Faith and the Leading of the Spirit

Notwithstanding this double disaster, the faith sons who enter the spirit kingdom and devote themselves to doing the Father's will experience less of the warfare between flesh and spirit [34:7.6]. Jesus showed a new way of mortal living whereby the consequences of the Caligastic rebellion may very largely be escaped and the deprivations resulting from the Adamic default most effectively compensated [34:7.6]. Those who are spirit-born and know God experience no more conflict than the inhabitants of the most normal worlds untainted by sin; they work on far higher intellectual levels and live on spiritual planes [34:7.7]. Throughout our lifetime the combined Spirit ever ministers to assist us in subjecting the flesh more and more to the leading of the Spirit [34:6.9].

5. Do Not Fear; Go Forward

The book counsels those who have started out on the way of life everlasting not to fear human forgetfulness and mortal inconstancy, and not to be troubled with doubts of failure [34:7.8]. And it gives the reason: in every dark hour and at every crossroad, the Spirit of Truth will always speak, saying, "⟦Q 34:7.8⟧This is the way⟦/Q⟧." [34:7.8]

Summary

The warfare between spirit and flesh is especially severe on Urantia because the Caligastia rebellion took away the moral support of society, and the Adamic default kept us from receiving a physical nature more responsive to spirit [34:7.4, 34:7.5]. Yet the natural appetites of the flesh are not in themselves in conflict with spiritual attainment [34:7.7], and the life of faith that enters the spirit kingdom and does the Father's will is the way to win this warfare [34:7.6]. As the book quotes, "⟦Q 34:7.6⟧This is the victory that overcomes the flesh, even your faith⟦/Q⟧." [34:7.6]

q196.question: How did the Melchizedek Sons of the local universe come into being, and why are they called "emergency Sons" and become teachers of mankind?
q196.answer:
The Melchizedek Sons are an order of local universe sonship that arises from the creative union of the Creator Son and the local universe Mother Spirit. First, from the union of these two, the original Melchizedek, the Father Melchizedek, was born, and he, collaborating with the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit, brought into being the entire group of that name [35:1.1]. The Melchizedeks of our universe were all created within a period of one thousand years of standard time, and their recorded number in Nebadon exceeds ten million [35:1.3, 35:2.9].

Among the divine Sons they are the first order to approach near enough to lower creatures to serve the evolutionary races without incarnation, and so they are Sons especially close to us [35:2.1].

1. Intermediaries between Higher and Lower Beings

The Melchizedeks are by nature at the mid-point of the great personality descent, so that they become the natural intermediaries between higher divine existence and material life [35:2.1]. The angels therefore delight to work with them, and all intelligent life finds in them "⟦Q 35:2.1⟧understanding friends, sympathetic teachers, and wise counselors⟦/Q⟧" [35:2.1]. The Father Melchizedek, as the first executive associate of Gabriel, presides over special and emergency commissions, and in Gabriel's absence he functions as the chief executive of Nebadon [35:1.2].

2. The Pattern of Self-government

The Melchizedeks are an order in which one of their own number functioned as a co-ordinate creator, so that they are partly self-originated, and they are an autonomous order that elects its own chief for a term of seven years [35:1.3]. The book says that in all Orvonton these Sons have never once betrayed a trust, and that they are the patterns and teachers of self-government for every sphere in Nebadon [35:2.2]. They occupy the place of the first-born in a great family, patrol the universe on their own initiative, and are unprejudiced observers who report to the Creator Son through their independent intelligence organization [35:2.3]. Yet though nearly perfect in wisdom, they are not infallible in judgment; when on rare occasions they make a minor error, they are instructed on Salvington and return to service on the third day [35:2.8].

3. Emergency Sons: The First Responders in a Crisis

The Melchizedeks are chiefly devoted to the educational system of the local universe, but they also act in special emergencies and are known on Edentia as "emergency Sons" [35:4.2]. Wherever special help is needed, one or more Melchizedeks are sure to be present, and when the plans of the Creator Son threaten to fail, a Melchizedek goes at once [35:4.2, 35:4.3]. They serve as temporary custodians on wayward planets or as receivers of defaulting planetary governments, and seven times in Nebadon they have served in the likeness of mortal flesh [35:4.4]. Melchizedek of Salem in the days of Abraham incarnated with the sanction of the receivers, who feared that the light of life would be extinguished, and handed on the truth to Abraham [35:4.5].

4. Teachers of the Ascenders and the Melchizedek University

The highly specialized work of the Melchizedeks is the supervision of the morontia career of ascending mortals, and together with the seraphim and the Trinity Teacher Sons they oversee their education [35:4.1]. The Melchizedek world near Salvington and its tributary spheres are called the "Melchizedek University," and every evolutionary mortal who has completed the constellation training lands here and is inducted into the Salvington educational system [35:3.1, 35:3.11]. The book says that even after we reach Paradise we will never forget our reactions on our first day on this world [35:3.11]. Moreover, when an Avonal Son makes a bestowal, twelve Melchizedeks accompany him as sponsors [35:2.6].

Summary

The Melchizedek Sons are the first-born order of the local universe, brought into being by the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit in collaboration with the Father Melchizedek [35:1.1, 35:2.3], and they serve as friends, teachers, and counselors at the midpoint between divinity and material life [35:2.1]. They are the pattern of self-government who have never betrayed a trust [35:2.2], the emergency Sons who are first to hasten to every crisis [35:4.2, 35:4.4], and the teachers of the Melchizedek University who instruct ascending mortals [35:3.11, 35:4.1].

q197.question: Why does rebellion in a local universe arise precisely among the Lanonandek Sons, and what kind of beings are they?
q197.answer:
The Lanonandek Sons are the third order of local universe sonship created by the Creator Son and the Universe Mother Spirit, after the Melchizedeks and the Vorondadeks. They are best known as System Sovereigns, the rulers of the local systems, and as Planetary Princes, the executive heads of the inhabited worlds [35:8.1]. Lanaforge, the present System Sovereign of Satania, is the successor of the apostate Lucifer [45:3.2], and Caligastia, the former Planetary Prince of our world, also belonged to this order as a Planetary Prince [49:5.23, 35:8.1], so this order is deeply entangled with the history of our planet.

The book explains that just as the Lanonandeks can draw nearer to lower creatures and render great service, so are they exposed to the greater danger of going astray and departing from the techniques of universe government [35:8.15]. The reason rebellion arises in this order lies precisely in the lowly position and the great freedom they have been given.

1. The Training and the Three Classes of Lanonandeks

The Lanonandeks, being a later-created order of lower divinity level, had to be trained as the first students of the Melchizedek University [35:8.2]. Nebadon started out with exactly twelve million Lanonandeks, and at the final examinations they were classified as primary, who become System Sovereigns and high counselors; secondary, who become Planetary Princes; and tertiary, who work as assistants, messengers, and custodians [35:8.3-8.6]. They cannot be advanced from one class to another, they do not reproduce, and their number is fixed [35:8.7]. The primary order in particular is the ablest and most versatile of all local universe administrators, surpassed in executive ability only by Gabriel and his associates [35:8.15].

2. The Almost Complete Authority of the System Sovereigns

The System Sovereigns rule in commissions of two or three [35:9.2]; they are well-nigh sovereign in the local affairs of the inhabited worlds and are almost paternal in their direction of the Planetary Princes, the Material Sons, and the ministering spirits [35:9.5]. They are not supervised by Trinity observers from the central universe [35:9.5]. The book therefore says that this position is, in all universe administration, "⟦Q 35:9.5⟧the one place in all universe administration where personal disloyalty to the will of the Michael Son could most easily and readily intrench itself and seek to assert itself⟦/Q⟧" [35:9.5], meaning personal disloyalty to the will of Michael.

3. The Rebellions in Nebadon and Their Meaning

In Nebadon more than seven hundred Lanonandek Sons have rebelled, but only three of them were System Sovereigns, and nearly all belonged to the secondary and tertiary orders [35:9.6]. Among the local universes of Orvonton, only Henselon has lost more of this order than ours [35:9.8]. But the book states clearly that this is not a defect of creatorship. They could have been made perfect, but they were created as they are in order to understand and draw nearer to the evolutionary creatures [35:9.7]. On Uversa it is held that our Lanonandeks have given so much trouble because they were created with great personal liberty, and it is maintained that the higher loyalty of the thoroughly tested Sons will more than compensate for the early confusion [35:9.8].

4. Dealing with Rebellion and the Way of Restoration

When rebellion occurs at a system headquarters, a new sovereign is installed within a comparatively short time, but this is not so on a planet [35:9.9]. When a Planetary Prince rebels, the planet is at once isolated and its local spiritual circuits are severed, and only a bestowal Son can re-establish those lines of communication [35:9.9]. The successor Planetary Prince does not assume actual rule until the consequences of the rebellion have been to some degree overcome by the corrective measures of the Melchizedeks and others [35:9.9]. There is also a plan for the salvage of the erring Sons, and many have availed themselves of this mercy, but they can never again function in the positions in which they defaulted [35:9.10].

Summary

The Lanonandek Sons are the capable administrative Sons of the local universe who serve as System Sovereigns and Planetary Princes [35:8.1, 35:8.15]; because they are close to lower creatures, were given great personal liberty, and rule almost sovereignly without the supervision of Trinity observers, they are the most exposed to the danger of rebellion [35:9.5, 35:9.8]. This danger is not a defect of creation but the price of a design intended to serve evolutionary creatures better [35:9.7], and it will in the end be compensated by the deeper loyalty of the Sons who have withstood the test [35:9.8].

q198.question: What are the Life Carriers, and what does it mean that although they make the forms of life, they cannot themselves give the "spark of life"?
q198.answer:
The Life Carriers are special Sons of the local universe who first plant and cultivate physical life on the evolving worlds. The book says, "⟦Q 36:3.1⟧Life does not spontaneously appear in the universes⟦/Q⟧" [36:3.1], and explains that their work is to initiate life on the barren planets. At the same time, it clearly distinguishes between what the Life Carriers can and cannot do. They organize the material forms and patterns of life, but the initial spark of life and the endowment of mind are supplied by spirit [36:6.3].

This distinction sums up the whole view of life in The Urantia Book. Life is not inherent in matter but is a gift from above [36:6.1].

1. The Unique Origin of the Life Carriers

The Life Carriers belong to the family of divine sonship, yet they are the only group of intelligent life within a local universe in whose creation the rulers of a superuniverse participate [36:1.1]. They are the offspring of three personalities: the Creator Son, the Universe Mother Spirit, and one of the Ancients of Days [36:1.1]. It is significant that the Ancients of Days, the only beings who can decree the extinction of intelligent life, participate in the creation of those who establish life [36:1.1]. One hundred million Life Carriers have been created in Nebadon, and they are directed by the life-determining trio of Gabriel, the Father Melchizedek, and Nambia, the first-born Life Carrier [36:1.2].

2. Life Is Given "through" Them

The Life Carriers prepare the physical patterns according to approved formulas and, acting as catalysts upon lifeless matter, impart the vital spirit spark [36:3.3]. But the book distinguishes that the spark of life is bestowed through the Life Carriers, not by them, and says that it is the Universe Mother Spirit who supplies the essential factor of living plasm [36:3.4]. In giving life they transmit nothing of their personal nature; they function only as a living catalytic presence [36:3.5].

3. Life Only from Life

The book says, "⟦Q 36:6.2⟧life springs only from life⟦/Q⟧" [36:6.2]. Mind can be derived only from pre-existent mind, and spirit takes origin only from spirit ancestors [36:6.2]. Therefore, however much more deeply human physics and chemistry may come to understand protoplasm, they will never produce living organisms [36:6.1]. Even the living forms the Life Carriers have produced experimentally on Salvington lack the endowment of mind and the power of reproduction, because mind is the gift of the Mother Spirit through the adjutant mind-spirits, and the power of reproduction is likewise imparted by the Universe Spirit [36:6.3]. The Sons of God construct the forms, but it is the Spirit of God who contributes the spark of life [36:6.4].

4. From Implantation to Withdrawal

The corps that plants life on a new world usually consists of one hundred senior carriers, one hundred assistants, and one thousand custodians [36:3.2], and it is granted a period of about half a million years [36:3.6]. Until human beings of moral status appear, they may manipulate the environment to favor evolution, but once will creatures are produced, their work is finished and they may no longer manipulate [36:3.7, 36:3.8]. They leave when the Planetary Prince arrives, but two senior carriers and twelve custodians may remain as advisers, and they are serving in this way on Urantia today [36:3.9].

5. The Mystery That Remains

The author of the book confesses that while the electrochemical formulas of the Life Carriers are fully comprehended, the nature and source of the life-activating spark are not wholly understood [36:6.7]. All that is known is that life flows from the Father through the Son and by the Spirit, and that "⟦Q 36:6.7⟧concept is inherent in the Father, expression in the Son, and life realization in the Spirit⟦/Q⟧" [36:6.7]. Plant and animal life do not survive death individually, and mortal survival depends on the evolution of an immortal soul within the mortal mind [36:6.5].

Summary

The Life Carriers, offspring of the Creator Son, the Mother Spirit, and an Ancient of Days, are the Sons who plant life on the evolutionary worlds [36:1.1, 36:3.1]. They organize the forms and patterns of life and act as catalysts, but the spark of life, mind, and the power of reproduction come from the Mother Spirit [36:3.4, 36:6.3], and life springs only from life [36:6.2]. This teaching shows that life is not a chance product of matter but a gift flowing from a divine source [36:6.7].

q199.question: What are the Brilliant Evening Stars and the archangels, and what does it mean that there is a headquarters of the archangels on Urantia?
q199.answer:
The Brilliant Evening Stars and the archangels are both high spirit beings of the local universe who come from the Creator Son and the Mother Spirit, but their work differs. The Brilliant Evening Stars are superangels who serve chiefly as liaison officers of Gabriel, the chief executive of the local universe [37:2.1], while the archangels are not concerned with the daily administration of the universe but are devoted to the work of creature survival and the furtherance of the ascending career of mortals [37:3.2].

In particular, Paper 37 reports the remarkable fact that our planet Urantia has become a divisional headquarters for certain archangel activities, and it connects this with Michael's bestowal [37:3.3, 37:3.4].

1. The Brilliant Evening Stars: Gabriel's Representatives

The Brilliant Evening Stars are beings planned by the Melchizedeks and brought into existence by the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit, and they function as Gabriel's representatives on all the constellation and system capitals of Nebadon [37:2.1]. Since Gabriel cannot be in two places at once, the Evening Stars compensate for this limitation [37:2.2], and when they have gone to individual planets on special assignments they have sometimes been known as "⟦Q 37:2.3⟧the angel of the Lord⟦/Q⟧" [37:2.3]. They are a unique dual order, made up of those of created dignity and ascendant spirits who have attained that status through service; of the 13,641 in the Nebadon corps, 8,809 are ascendant, and many of these began their careers as seraphim [37:2.4]. When they receive an assignment, they always work in pairs, a created Evening Star with an ascendant one [37:2.7].

2. Evening Stars Who Accompany the Bestowal Sons

One of the high duties of the Evening Stars is to accompany the Avonal bestowal Sons on their planetary missions, even as Gabriel accompanied Michael on his Urantia bestowal [37:2.8]. These superangels become cocommanders of such missions, and it is the senior of them who bids the Avonal Son, "⟦Q 37:2.8⟧Be about your brother's business⟦/Q⟧." [37:2.8] Gavalia, the first-born, is the chief of this order, and Galantia, the first ascendant superangel, has his headquarters on Jerusem [37:2.6].

3. The Archangels: Ministers of Survival and Resurrection

The archangels are the highest type of high spirit being produced in large numbers in the local universe; there are nearly eight hundred thousand of them in Nebadon, and they are usually not under the jurisdiction of Gabriel [37:3.1, 37:3.2]. A corps of one hundred archangels accompanies every Paradise bestowal Son to an inhabited world [37:3.5], and two senior archangels are assigned as the personal aids of an Avonal [37:3.6]. When the dead are called forth at the end of a dispensation, it is literally true that the seraphic guardians of the slumbering personalities respond to "⟦Q 37:3.6⟧the voice of the archangel⟦/Q⟧," and this archangel is called the archangel of the resurrection or the "archangel of Michael" [37:3.6]. On the archangels' world at Salvington the personality recorders preserve the records of the mortal ascension career from birth, and during the interval between death and resurrection they keep the personality records and identity specifications [37:3.7, 37:3.8].

4. The Archangels' Divisional Headquarters on Urantia

The archangel corps of Nebadon is directed by the first-born archangel, and more recently a divisional headquarters of the archangels has been maintained on Urantia [37:3.3]. Student visitors from other universes are surprised that archangel activities are directed from such a small and seemingly insignificant world, but when they learn of Michael's bestowal, their interest in our planet is at once heightened [37:3.3]. The book says that this fact presages the future concentration of other ascendant activities on Michael's bestowal world and lends a solemn import to the Master's promise, "⟦Q 37:3.4⟧I will come again⟦/Q⟧." [37:3.4]

Summary

The Brilliant Evening Stars are superangels who represent Gabriel in liaison and special missions throughout the universe, working in pairs of the created and the ascendant [37:2.1, 37:2.7]. The archangels are high spirit beings in charge of mortal survival and resurrection and the preservation of personality records [37:3.6, 37:3.8], and the presence of their divisional headquarters on Urantia, Michael's bestowal world, is a sign that our planet will hold a special place in the future ascension activities of the universe [37:3.4].

q200.question: What is the nature of the seraphic angels? Please explain whether they have emotions or sex, how they treat human beings, and whether it is right to worship angels.
q200.answer:
Paper 38 of The Urantia Book explains in detail the origin and nature of the seraphim, the ministering spirits of our local universe. The seraphim are created by the Universe Mother Spirit; since the early days of Nebadon they have been projected in unit formations of 41,472 at a time [38:1.1], and because the universe is still in the making, they are still being created periodically [38:1.3].

The angels the book portrays are not cold transcendent beings but companions who understand and love us. They have no material bodies, yet they are definite and discrete beings, of spirit nature and origin [38:2.1].

1. Beings Who Know and Understand Us

Angels are invisible to mortals, but they perceive us as we are in the flesh without the aid of transformers or translators [38:2.1]. They intellectually understand the mode of mortal life, share all of man's nonsensuous emotions and sentiments, and appreciate and greatly enjoy our efforts in music, art, and real humor [38:2.1]. They are also fully cognizant of our moral struggles and spiritual difficulties. The book says, "⟦Q 38:2.1⟧They love human beings, and only good can result from your efforts to understand and love them⟦/Q⟧." [38:2.1]

2. Sex and Emotion

Seraphim are exceedingly affectionate and sympathetic beings, but they are not creatures of sex emotion [38:2.2]. They are very much like what we will be on the mansion worlds, where we will neither marry nor be given in marriage but will be like the angels [38:2.2]. On worlds of sex, however, angels are usually referred to with feminine pronouns, following the custom of calling the spirit children the daughters of God [38:2.2].

3. Remarkable Abilities, Yet Close Companions

Seraphim are created to function on both spiritual and literal levels, so that there are few morontia and spirit activities not open to them [38:2.3]. In personal status they are not so far removed from human beings, but in certain functions they far transcend humans. For example, they have an inherent ability to know such things as the number of the hairs on one's head, and the book says that we would regard them as veritable mathematical prodigies [38:2.3]. In nature and personality endowment they are only slightly in advance of the mortal races, and when we are delivered from the flesh we become very much like them [38:2.6]. On the mansion worlds we will begin to understand them, on the constellation spheres we will enjoy them, and on Salvington we will share their places of rest and worship [38:2.6].

4. Neither Judges nor Objects of Worship

Angels are superior to us in spiritual status, but they are not our judges or accusers [38:2.4]. The book adds that just as the angels do not judge mankind, neither should we prejudge our fellow creatures [38:2.4]. It also makes clear: "⟦Q 38:2.5⟧You do well to love them, but you should not adore them⟦/Q⟧" [38:2.5]. When the seer fell down before her feet, the great seraphim Loyalatia said that she was a fellow servant with those who are all enjoined to worship God [38:2.5].

5. Trained Ministering Spirits

The seraphim spend their first millennium as observers on Salvington and their second in training on the seraphic worlds, and the Melchizedeks also have a large part in their education [38:5.1]. They are then initiated as observers on the lowest evolutionary worlds, complete their training on the architectural worlds of the system capitals, and are commissioned as ministering spirits [38:5.3]. Their work is to bring the beings of the spirit world into contact with the mortals of the material realms [38:5.4].

Summary

The seraphim are individual spirit beings created by the Mother Spirit who perceive us as we are, understand our emotions and struggles, and love us [38:1.1, 38:2.1]. They have deep affection but are not creatures of sex emotion [38:2.2], and though they have remarkable abilities, they are close companions and our future brethren [38:2.3, 38:2.6]. Angels do not judge us, and they are to be loved, not worshiped [38:2.4, 38:2.5].

q201.question: Do angels also ascend and reach Paradise? Please explain the destiny of the seraphim, Seraphington, and the Seraphic Corps of Completion.
q201.answer:
Yes. The Urantia Book teaches that the seraphim, who originate in the local universes, also walk the path to God. Some achieve service destiny within their native local universe, and some are elevated to Brilliant Evening Stars, but the book says, "⟦Q 39:8.1⟧Seraphington ever remains the eternal goal of all angels⟦/Q⟧." [39:8.1] Seraphington is the angelic threshold to Paradise and Deity attainment, the transition sphere from the ministry of time to the service of eternity [39:8.1].

In particular, the fact that serving as guardian angels of mortals is the path of ascension the angels most desire shows how deeply our destiny and that of the angels are interwoven [39:8.5].

1. Three Principal Paths to Paradise

Seraphim may attain Paradise by numerous methods, but the book names three representative paths [39:8.2]. The first is to achieve perfection in specialized service as celestial artisans, technical advisers, or celestial recorders, and so enter Paradise [39:8.3]. The second is to be summoned to Seraphington; no seraphim may set out on its own, but must patiently wait for a Paradise messenger of the tertiary supernaphim to bring the summons [39:8.4]. The third is to attain by the technique of evolutionary mortals, and in the career of time the supreme choice of the seraphim is the office of guardian angel [39:8.5].

2. Guardians of Destiny: Angels Who Ascend with Mortals

These personal guides of the children of time are called guardians of destiny, because in guarding mortal creatures on the path of divine destiny they determine their own high destiny [39:8.5]. They are chosen from among the more experienced angels, and all mortal ascenders have permanent seraphic associates before leaving the mansion worlds [39:8.6]. Because angels are created "a little higher" than we are, they cannot ascend to God from the human level, but it has been wisely arranged that they may go down to those who start from the bottom and pilot them, world by world, to the portals of Havona [39:8.7]. When mortals depart for Havona, the guardians bid them a temporary farewell and on Seraphington attempt, and undoubtedly achieve, the seven circles of seraphic light [39:8.7].

3. Seraphington: The Destiny Sphere of the Angels

All evolutionary seraphim pass through Seraphington regardless of their path of ascent, and the majority pass through this experience instead of the Havona circuits [39:8.8]. Angels are not sure of their eternal future until they arrive on Seraphington, but no angel attaining Seraphington has ever been known to go astray [39:8.9]. The book says, "⟦Q 39:8.9⟧sin will never find response in the heart of a seraphim of completion⟦/Q⟧." [39:8.9] Among the graduates, the guardians of destiny who have had the Havona circle experience generally enter the Mortal Corps of the Finality, while others are mustered into the corps of nonmortal finaliters or the Seraphic Corps of Completion [39:8.10]. The "adopted seraphim" of the Corps of the Finality are guardian angels who have ascended together with their wards in this way [31:4.1].

4. The Seraphic Corps of Completion

The angels who have attained the Father of spirits and been received into the service of completion are those who have experientially compensated for the difference in divinity potential that formerly distinguished them from the ministering spirits of the central universe and the superuniverses [39:9.1]. For them the career of time is ended; they are henceforth and forever the servants of God and the associates of the Paradise finaliters [39:9.1]. Many seraphim of completion return to their native universes to supplement the ministry of divine endowment with the ministry of experiential perfection, and Urantia too enjoys the ministry of the twelve specialized groups of this corps [39:9.2]. Even after Paradise they most desire to serve as attendants of the bestowal Sons, and they are always our true friends and unfailing helpers [39:9.3].

Summary

The seraphim also attain Paradise, by the paths of perfection in specialized service, summons to Seraphington, and the guardian of destiny who ascends together with mortals [39:8.3-8.5]. All evolutionary seraphim pass through Seraphington, the destiny sphere of the angels, and an angel who reaches it never goes astray [39:8.8, 39:8.9]. The seraphim of completion serve forever as associates of the finaliters, and even now they are friends who help our ascent [39:9.1, 39:9.3].

q202.question: How do Father-fused, Son-fused, and Spirit-fused mortals differ, and is it not discrimination that their destinies differ?
q202.answer:
Paper 40 of The Urantia Book explains that surviving mortals are divided into three classes according to the spirit with which they fuse. The great majority are Father-fused mortals, who fuse with the Thought Adjuster, a fragment of the Universal Father; there are also, rarely, Son-fused mortals, who fuse with the spirit of the Creator Son, and Spirit-fused mortals, who fuse with an individualization of the local universe Mother Spirit [40:7.1, 40:8.3, 40:9.3]. There is no overlapping in fusion experience, so a will creature is only one of these three [40:9.1].

The book stresses repeatedly that this difference in destiny is by no means a matter of superiority and inferiority. That destinies vary proves "⟦Q 40:10.5⟧merely that they differ⟦/Q⟧" [40:10.5], and there is no favoritism and nothing arbitrary in the divine plan of mortal survival.

1. Father-fused Mortals: Those Bound for Paradise
