The Adjuster is an immortal spirit, and union with it confers eternal life upon the fused soul [40:7.1]. Practically all surviving mortals fuse with their Adjusters on the mansion worlds or on the higher morontia spheres [40:8.1]. Our race also belongs to this group, and when we and our Adjusters at last become one, we become ascending sons of God, just as the Son of God and the Son of Man became one in Michael [40:7.2]. Fusion with a fragment of the Father is the divine guarantee of eventual Paradise attainment, and these are the order of humans who pass through Havona and find God on Paradise [40:7.5].

2. Son-fused Mortals: Those Who Failed of Fusion through No Fault of Their Own

A few fail to fuse with their Adjusters despite the "seventy times seven" opportunities [40:8.2]. When it becomes evident that some difficulty of attunement is preventing fusion, the survival adjudicators are convened, and if the mortal is adjudged not to be at fault, the Adjuster returns to Divinington and the mortal fuses with an individualized gift of the spirit of the Creator Son [40:8.3]. There are fewer than one million of them in Orvonton, and they are in every respect equal to their Adjuster-fused fellows except in the destiny of Paradise residence [40:8.5].

3. Spirit-fused Mortals: Permanent Citizens of the Local Universe

Spirit fusion does not take place during the natural life; it occurs upon reawakening on the mansion worlds, when an individualization of the Mother Spirit takes the place of the departed Adjuster [40:9.1, 40:9.3]. In these mortals too the Adjuster builds up the soul during the life in the flesh, but after death it takes leave of them forever [40:9.2]. They therefore awaken without consciousness of their former existence, and with the help of the seraphim and the recording angels they come to repossess much of their memory [40:9.4, 40:9.5]. They are permanent citizens of the local universe, and the eighth group of worlds surrounding Salvington is their home [40:9.9].

4. Spirits That Ascend to Their Own Level of Origin

Spirit-fused mortals are limited to the local universe and Son-fused survivors to the superuniverse, while Adjuster-fused mortals are destined to traverse the universe of universes [40:10.1]. This is because the spirits that fuse with mortals always ascend to their own level of origin [40:10.1]. The book explains that if all mortals were sent to Paradise, the local universe and superuniverse governments would depend solely on the service of those passing through, so it is entirely fitting that there be a permanent ascending citizenry [40:10.4]. The Spirit-fused veterans accumulate an intimate knowledge and authoritative wisdom about a universe and contribute decisively to its settling [40:10.6]. Moreover, some Son-fused and Spirit-fused beings do, after certain changes, actually ascend to Paradise [40:10.10].

5. The Father's Equal Love

The book says that it would be hardly proper to contrast the destinies of the ascending sons as "greater" or "lesser" [40:10.13]. The Father loves each of his sons individually and personally, and "⟦Q 40:10.13⟧Sonship is the supreme relationship of the creature to the Creator⟦/Q⟧." [40:10.13]

Summary

Father-fused mortals fuse with the Adjuster and go to Paradise; Son-fused mortals, after a failure of fusion for which they are not at fault, fuse with the spirit of the Son and serve permanently in the superuniverse; and Spirit-fused mortals fuse with the Mother Spirit and serve permanently in the local universe [40:7.5, 40:8.5, 40:9.9]. This difference is not one of superiority but of different destinies of service needed in universe administration [40:10.4, 40:10.5], and God loves all his sons alike [40:10.13].

q203.question: How does The Urantia Book explain what makes the sun shine, how long it will shine, and how stars grow old and die?
q203.answer:
Paper 41 of The Urantia Book introduces our sun as one of the more than two thousand suns of Satania, "⟦Q 41:3.1⟧an average blazing orb⟦/Q⟧" [41:3.1], and explains in some detail the sources of solar energy and the life of the sun. According to the book, the sun derives its energy not from one source but from seven [41:7.3]; its stability depends on the balance between gravity and heat [41:9.4]; and our sun will go on shining at its present efficiency for more than twenty-five billion years [41:9.5].

The book also says that the age of a star can be estimated from its color and size, and explains that even dying stars can be revived in several ways [41:3.7, 41:7.15].

1. The Interior of the Sun

The surface temperature of the sun is almost 6,000 degrees Fahrenheit, but it rises rapidly toward the interior until at the center it reaches about 35,000,000 degrees [41:7.2]. Practically no whole atoms exist in the interior of the sun, and because the intensive X-ray bombardment renders the elements very similar, the book says, "⟦Q 41:7.1⟧Le rayon X est le grand niveleur de l’existence atomique.⟦/Q⟧." [41:7.1] At such temperatures and pressures atoms are broken up into electrons and other constituents, yet even the sun cannot disrupt the ultimatons themselves [41:7.12]. A regulating blanket of hot gases surrounding the sun stabilizes its heat loss [41:7.11].

2. The Seven Sources of Solar Energy

The book lists the seven sources in order of importance [41:7.3]: annihilation of atoms and eventually of electrons; transmutation of elements, including radioactive energy; the accumulation and transmission of certain universal space energies; space matter and meteors diving into the sun; solar contraction; the action of gravity at high temperatures transforming certain circuitized power into radiant energies; and recaptured light and matter [41:7.4-7.10]. The amount of heat our solar system's sun gives off each second is sufficient to boil all the waters of all the oceans of Urantia in just one second [41:7.13].

3. Stability and Lifespan

The stability of the sun depends wholly on the equilibrium between the contention of gravity and heat, that is, the balance of tremendous pressures against unimaginable temperatures [41:9.4]. In young stars, when this equilibrium is upset, they may correct the imbalance by throwing off their outer layers into space [41:9.4]. The center of our sun is discharging almost one hundred billion tons of actual matter each year [41:9.3], and it long ago attained a relative equilibrium between its cycles of expansion and contraction [41:9.5]. The sun is now passing its six billionth year, in its most economical period, and it will shine as it now does for more than twenty-five billion years before entering a long period of decline [41:9.5].

4. The Age and Color of Stars

Most of the giant suns are relatively young and most of the dwarf stars are old, but not all [41:3.7]. Very young and very old suns are usually red; yellow indicates moderate youth or approaching old age; and brilliant white signifies robust and extended adult life [41:3.7]. Our sun bears a legacy of its youthful pulsations, whose period has lengthened from three and one-half days to the present eleven and one-half year sunspot cycle [41:3.8].

5. The Death and Rebirth of Stars

Only suns that lie in the path of the main currents of universe energy receive space-force to replenish their loss of matter and may shine on forever, while distant stars eventually cool and go out [41:7.14]. But dead or dying suns may be recharged by collisional impact, by certain nonluminous energy islands of space, or by gravity-robbery of near-by suns, and the majority of dead suns are revived in this way [41:7.15]. A sun that is not eventually recharged collapses by mass explosion at the critical level of ultimatonic condensation and becomes a rare form of energy that supplies other suns [41:7.15, 41:3.6].

Summary

According to The Urantia Book, the sun derives its energy from seven sources, beginning with the annihilation of atoms and electrons [41:7.3-7.10]; it maintains its stability through the balance of gravity and heat [41:9.4]; and our sun will shine as it now does for more than twenty-five billion years to come [41:9.5]. Stars grow old and go out, but most are regenerated, and even a star that vanishes becomes energy for other stars and takes part in the energy cycle of the universe [41:7.15].

q204.question: What does the passage "the spirit is the architect, the mind is the builder, the body is the material building" mean, and do spirit beings also have form?
q204.answer:
This passage appears in the last section of Paper 42 of The Urantia Book, the section on patterns and forms and the dominance of mind [42:12.12]. Just before it the book says, "⟦Q 42:12.12⟧Sur un monde matériel, vous pensez à un corps comme ayant un esprit, mais nous, nous considérons l’esprit comme pourvu d’un corps.⟦/Q⟧." [42:12.12] That is, it is not that the body is the master and the spirit an addition to it, but rather that the spirit designs, the mind builds form according to that design, and the body is the house erected as the result.

This view connects with the conclusion of Paper 42 as a whole, that the universe is neither machine nor magic but "⟦Q 42:11.1⟧a creation of mind and a mechanism of law⟦/Q⟧" [42:11.1], and it extends into the teaching that spirit beings also have real forms [42:12.10].

1. Mind Is Ever Creative

The book says that the very fact that mechanisms evolve points to a creative mind that hiddenly dominates them [42:12.1]. Mind reaches out from the creation of material mechanisms through the discovery of mystery, the establishment of philosophic systems, and the achievement of wisdom and spirit levels, to the achievement of divine destiny [42:12.2-12.8]. And whether in animal, mortal, morontian, or spirit ascender, the mind endowment is always able to produce a body suitable for the identity of that creature [42:12.9]. Personality form is the pattern aspect of a living being, the arrangement of energies, and this, plus life and motion, is the mechanism of creature existence [42:12.9].

2. Spirit Beings Also Have Form

The book says, "⟦Q 42:12.10⟧Even spirit beings have form, and these spirit forms (patterns) are real⟦/Q⟧." [42:12.10] Even the highest spirit personalities have personality presences in every sense analogous to mortal bodies, and nearly all beings in the seven superuniverses possess forms [42:12.10]. There are exceptions: Thought Adjusters appear to be without form until after fusion with the souls of mortals, and some beings, such as Solitary Messengers, Gravity Messengers, and Transcendental Recorders, are also without discoverable form, but these are the exceptional few [42:12.10].

3. From Body to Morontia Form to Spirit Form

Just as the ministry of the cosmic mind and the adjutant mind-spirits evolves the physical tabernacle of evolving man, so the morontia mind individualizes the morontia forms of survivors [42:12.11]. No two morontia forms are more alike than two human bodies, and the form reveals the creative mind that dominates it [42:12.11]. Morontia material is sponsored by the Morontia Power Supervisors and supplied by the seraphim, and the subsequent spirit forms likewise characteristically reveal the indwelling spirit-mind [42:12.11]. Therefore the book calls the material eyes "⟦Q 42:12.12⟧the windows of the spirit-born soul⟦/Q⟧" [42:12.12].

4. The Primacy of Spirit and the Choice of Mind

Physical, mindal, and spiritual energies are co-ordinate on Paradise and co-ordinated in Havona, but in time and space physical energy appears to be dominant; as spirit-mind function approaches divinity, spirit becomes more dominant, and on absolute levels spirit is unquestionably dominant [42:12.13]. Wherever true spirit-mind functions, there tends to be its material counterpart, for the physical is the time-space reflection of spirit reality [42:12.13, 42:12.14]. The book says that "⟦Q 42:12.15⟧Mind universally dominates matter⟦/Q⟧" [42:12.15] and is responsive to the ultimate overcontrol of spirit, and it concludes that only the mind that freely submits itself to spirit direction can hope for eternal survival [42:12.15].

Summary

This passage speaks of the order of reality in which the spirit designs, the mind builds, and the body is the result [42:12.12]. Mind always produces a body suited to its identity, and spirit beings too have real, individual forms [42:12.9, 42:12.10]. The transformation from our body to morontia form and spirit form also follows this principle [42:12.11], and in the end it is the mind that freely follows the leading of the spirit that opens the way to eternal survival [42:12.15].
